# **Mobile build in Lovable**

Build FairFlow in Lovable one screen per prompt, phone-first at 390 px wide, against sample data, then connect real data. This tab walks through every screen as a superintendent sees it on a phone, then gives the prompts in the order to paste them.

Lovable generates a React, TypeScript and Tailwind app and connects to Supabase for sign-in, database, file storage and server functions. In this plan Lovable builds everything, including the weather fetch, the water balance engine and the advisor, as Supabase edge functions. An engine check page replaces unit tests.

## **Mobile walkthrough, login onward**

Each screen is described top to bottom as it appears on a phone held in one hand. Thumb-reach actions sit in the bottom third.

### **1\. Splash and sign in (S1)**

* **Top half:** FairFlow wordmark in serif on deep green, tagline "Know which zones need water before you leave the shop."  
* **Bottom half (ivory card):** email field, "Send me a sign-in link" (primary, 56 px), divider, "Continue with Google".  
* **After tapping send:** "Check your email on this phone" with the address shown and a "Use a different email" link.  
* **Invite link:** skips this screen's choices and shows "Join U-M Golf Course as Crew" with one Join button.

### **2\. Course details (S2, step 1 of 3\)**

* **Top:** progress bar with the step names (Details, Map, Check), each tappable once reached; Back on every later step; "Finish later" saves progress.  
* **Course:** type the name; the address fills in and sets the weather location.  
* **Holes:** three large chips, 9, 18 and 27\.  
* **Optional,** collapsed: water source, water price and controller brand, with "Skip for now".  
* **Bottom:** Next.

### **3\. Upload a map (S2, step 2 of 3\)**

* **Upload area** filling the top half: "Take a photo or upload". It takes an irrigation map, course layout or scorecard, as a photo or PDF. No drawing.  
* **While reading:** a progress bar and what's been found so far ("Found 12 holes so far").  
* **Bottom:** "No map? Use a standard layout", built from the hole count.

### **4\. Check your course (S3, step 3 of 3\)**

* **Totals:** "18 holes · 54 zones · 108 valves", all filled in.  
* **Things to check:** an amber card with only the items the AI was unsure of, each a one-tap question ("Hole 7 green: 2 or 3 valves?").  
* **Holes** as collapsible rows; tap to fix a zone or valve. Areas and sprinkler output show an "Estimate" tag until changed.  
* **Bottom:** "Looks right". Corrections can also be spoken.

### **5\. First briefing**

* "Looks right" runs the first calculation and opens Home with the first briefing.  
* An optional card on Home offers an irrigation history CSV, saying it makes the first calls more accurate.

### **6\. Home: talk or type (S4)**

* **Header (deep green):** course name, today's date, "Updated 5:30 am".  
* **Morning briefing,** first in the feed: "Morning. Green 1 and Green 3 need water tonight, 8 to 12 minutes on each valve. Fairway 7 needs a look: its weather data is a day old. Everything else holds." After a night with runs, it starts with "Did last night's runs go as planned?" and a one-tap "Yes, all ran". Zone names are links. Under it: "Water 4 · Hold 11 · Check 2 · See all zones".  
* **Feed:** entries, questions and replies like a chat thread, newest at the bottom.  
* **Ask anything:** "Why is Fairway 7 on check?" gets a two-sentence answer with the numbers and a link to the zone, plus thumbs up or down.  
* **Prompt chips:** "Rain in the gauge?", "How do the greens look?", "What changed since yesterday?".  
* **Composer, in thumb reach:** a 64 px mic beside "Tell Mac or ask anything"; the keyboard's own dictation works in the text field too. "Use a form instead" sits under it.  
* **Bottom tab bar:** Home, Zones, Map, Notes, Community. Settings sits behind a profile button at the top right.

### **7\. Zone detail (S6)**

* **Top:** back arrow, zone name, status chip and confidence.  
* **Valves:** "3A · Water · 8 to 12 min", "3B · Water · 10 to 14 min"; swipe a row to Follow that valve.  
* **Show the math:** "47% − 0.21 in ET \+ 0.10 in rain \= 41%, threshold 45%" with the soil-water bar.  
* **Track record:** "Agreed with you on 34 of 45 days".  
* **Inputs:** ET, rain, irrigation, soil and slope, each with value, source and age.  
* **History:** a 14-day line per valve; tap a day to see that day's stored call.  
* **Ask about this zone,** then a sticky bottom bar: Follow all valves and Override, equal size.

### **8\. Override and Quick log (S7, S8)**

* Both open as bottom sheets over the zone, so context stays visible.  
* **Override:** status chips, amount stepper, reason chips, mic for a spoken reason, Save.  
* **Quick log:** four tabs (Rain, Irrigation, Hand check, Turf) with large buttons and a number pad; one tap saves.

### **9\. Here's what I heard (S9)**

* **While speaking:** waveform and timer over the composer; release or tap Stop. The feed shows "Working it out…".  
* **Within 3 seconds** a sheet slides up titled "Here's what I heard", with the transcript collapsed at the top.  
* **One row per item,** large numbers first: "Rain 0.50 in · whole course · today", "Green 3 · drier than expected", "Green 3 · turf slightly dry". Each row has edit and remove.  
* **Unsure items** show in amber with choices: "Which green? 1 · 3 · 7".  
* **Confirm** fills the bottom of the sheet (56 px). After it, the sheet closes and FairFlow replies in the feed: "Got it. Green 3 moves to Water, 8 to 12 minutes tonight. Everything else holds."  
* **No signal:** "Saved on phone · waiting for signal" in the feed; the confirm card appears once it's back.

### **10\. Zones, Notes, Crew home, Settings and Water use**

* **Zones (S14):** summary counts as filters, zones grouped Check, Water, Hold; swipe right to Follow, tap for Zone detail. Managers start here, read-only.  
* **Notes and issues (S10):** filter chips (Open, Mine, zone, type), then cards with author, time, zone, transcript and a play button. Swipe to mark done; tap to make a task.  
* **Crew home (S11):** the same composer and feed, their assigned tasks, and the zones to hand-water or check today; no Follow or Override.  
* **Settings (S12):** grouped list: My criteria, Team, Data, Notifications, Water use, Display (light, dark, automatic), Language, Read replies aloud, Sign out.  
* **Water use (S13):** season gallons and cost at the top, weekly bar chart, followed vs overridden, Export.

### **Mobile rules that apply everywhere**

* Design at 390 x 844 (iPhone 14); check at 360 px wide (small Android) and 768 px (tablet).  
* Respect the safe areas above and below (notch, home bar).  
* Bottom sheets instead of new pages for quick actions; back gestures always work.  
* Number pads for numbers (inputMode="decimal"); no tiny dropdowns.  
* Skeleton rows while loading; the last cached Today shows instantly.

## **Before you start in Lovable**

Five setup steps save rework later. Lovable's features change often, so confirm menu names against its docs as you go.

1. **Create one Lovable project** named FairFlow, and connect it to a GitHub repository from the start, so you have a backup and history outside Lovable.  
2. **Connect Supabase** from inside Lovable. It provides sign-in (email link and Google), the database, file storage for audio and photos, and server functions for anything that needs an API key. Add your Anthropic API key, plus a transcription key if used, to Supabase secrets.  
3. **Add project knowledge.** Lovable lets you save standing instructions for a project. Paste the "Project rules" prompt below there, so every later prompt follows the same design system without repeating it.  
4. **Build with sample data first.** Every screen reads from one sample course (6 zones, 14 days of history) until the engine is ready. Label it "Sample course" on screen.  
5. **Preview on your phone, not just the browser.** Open the preview link on a real phone after each prompt; resize-to-mobile in a desktop browser misses safe areas, keyboard covering fields, and sunlight readability.

**How to prompt Lovable well**

* To save credits, send the five batched messages below instead of the step-by-step prompts. Check each batch on a phone before sending the next.  
* Name the screen ID from the PRD ("Build S4 Today") so you and your teammates can trace changes.  
* When something is wrong, describe what you see and what you expected, rather than "fix it".  
* If Lovable breaks something that worked, use its version history to roll back rather than prompting around the damage.

## **Batched build: five messages**

This builds the whole MVP in five build messages instead of 22\. The PRD holds the design requirements (what to build and how it looks); the step-by-step prompts further down this tab hold the technical detail (tables, functions, constants). Lovable reads both from the repo, so each batch stays short.

**Set up once (no build credits beyond the first read):**

1. Paste prompt 0 (Project rules) into Lovable's project knowledge.  
2. Export the PRD tab and this tab as Markdown (Export menu under the doc's name) and upload them to the GitHub repo as docs/PRD.md and docs/BUILD.md.  
3. Send the read-through message below, in chat or plan mode if your plan has one.

I've added docs/PRD.md (product and design requirements for FairFlow) and docs/BUILD.md (numbered build steps with technical detail). Read both fully but don't build anything yet. Reply with: (1) a one-paragraph summary of the product, (2) the Supabase tables you'll create, and (3) any requirement that is unclear or contradicts another. I'll then send five batched build messages. For every design detail, follow docs/PRD.md; for tables, functions and constants, follow docs/BUILD.md.  
**Batch 1: foundation and demo**

Build steps 1, 2, 3 and 16 from docs/BUILD.md: the app shell and design system, the full Supabase schema with row-level security, sign-in and roles, and demo mode. Seed the demo course so every later step can be tested on it. Follow docs/PRD.md for all design details (Visual system, Users and roles, F11, F20, S1, S18). Don't build other screens yet. When done, list what you built, anything you skipped or changed and why, and how to open the demo.  
Check before batch 2: open the demo link on a phone; the banner, role switch and sign-in work.

**Batch 2: weather, engine and data**

Build steps 5a, 5b and 5c from docs/BUILD.md: the weather function, the versioned engine with recommendation records (including the extra flags and the short-water priority), the engine check page, the daily schedules, and optional data uploads (docs/PRD.md F2, F4, F9, F16, F18, F21). Run the engine over all 30 demo days. Only add to the schema what these need. Report the engine version and the engine check results.  
Check before batch 3: the engine check matches your hand-calculated examples, and demo recommendations exist for every valve.

**Batch 3: setup**

Build steps 4 and 5 from docs/BUILD.md: course details, map upload with the read-map function, the standard-layout fallback, and Check your course, with Back, tappable step names and Finish later (docs/PRD.md F1, S2, S3). Report anything you skipped.  
Check before batch 4: upload a real course map and see what the AI finds.

**Batch 4: the daily loop with Mac**

Build steps 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 10a from docs/BUILD.md: Home with Mac's briefing, feed and composer; Zones list; Zone detail with valves, the math and "Where's this from?"; the Override and Quick log sheets; the Map view; the transcribe, parse and confirm flow; and write-briefing and ask-advisor with Mac's persona and About card (docs/PRD.md F5 to F7, F12, F13, F17, F21, S4 to S9, S14). Show demo data everywhere. Report anything you skipped.  
Check before batch 5: say "half an inch in the gauge, Green 3 is dry", confirm, and read Mac's reply; ask "Why is Green 3 on water?"

**Batch 5: team, community and finish**

Build steps 11, 11b, 12, 13, 14 and 15 from docs/BUILD.md: Notes and issues, Crew home, Community with Translate, Settings (criteria with Water is short and turf priority, team, data, notifications, display, language, read aloud), Water use, the installable web app with no-signal behavior, and in-app alerts (docs/PRD.md F10, F11, F14, F15, F19, S10 to S13, S16, S17). Then check every screen against docs/PRD.md and list anything that doesn't match.  
**Fixes, batched too.** Collect everything wrong after a batch into one message, numbered, with the screen and what you expected. One fix list costs far less than a message per problem.

## **Lovable prompts, in build order**

Paste these one at a time and check each on a phone before the next. Run them in order: 0 to 5 lay foundations and setup; 5a to 5c build the weather data, the engine and the engine check; 6 to 10a build the talking and advisor experience; 11 to 16 finish the app, including demo mode.

### **0\. Project rules (save as project knowledge)**

You are building FairFlow, a mobile-first web app that advises golf course superintendents, valve by valve each morning, whether to water, hold or check, and why. Always follow these rules:

Advisor: the advisor is Mac, an AI character who talks like a calm retired superintendent, in the first person, with an illustrated avatar (original art, not a real person). Mac is always labeled AI and never claims to be human. Every assumption stores its source, date and who set it, so Mac can say where any number came from. Each morning it writes a short briefing. People can ask it anything about the calls; answers use only stored records and name their numbers and sources. One message in, one answer out: at most one follow-up, as tap choices.

Core interaction: Home is a mic and a text box. People speak or type what they see. An AI step turns it into items; a "Here's what I heard" card shows them; nothing is saved until the user taps Confirm; then FairFlow replies in one or two lines naming what changed. The AI only extracts and phrases; it never calculates water. Forms are a backup.

Structure: courses have zones; zones have valves (controller stations). Every call is per valve and stored as a recommendation record that is never overwritten.

Engine: the water balance lives in one Supabase edge function with a version number. Never change it while working on screens unless the prompt says so. Bump the version whenever it changes.

Layout: design for a 390 px wide phone first; also support 360 px and tablet (768 px+, two columns). Respect iOS/Android safe areas. Primary actions in the bottom third. Touch targets at least 48 px; primary buttons 56 px tall. Use bottom sheets for quick actions.

Visual style: premium private-club feel. Brand deep green \#1F3D2B, ivory surface \#F7F4EC, brass accent \#9C7A3C, white cards with a 1 px hairline border and 12 px radius, no heavy shadows. Headings in Source Serif 4 semibold; everything else in Inter with tabular numbers. Body 16 px, nothing below 14 px.

Status colors (never use green for a status): water \= blue \#1D5FA8 with a droplet icon; hold \= gray \#5F6670 with a pause icon; check \= amber fill \#F2A900 with dark text and a warning-triangle icon. Always show status as color \+ icon \+ word.

Dark mode: support light, dark and automatic (follow the device; default). Dark surfaces are deep green-black \#0F1A14 and \#18261D, text \#E9EEE9, water \#6AAFF2, check \#F5C04A, hold \#A7AEB8, brand sage \#8FB89A. Define all colors as Tailwind theme tokens / CSS variables, never hard-coded in components.

Accessibility: WCAG AA contrast, screen-reader labels on every control, supports large system text.

Language: the app, speech and replies work in English and Spanish; detect the spoken language automatically and reply in the user's chosen language. Writing: short and plain, like a colleague. Lead with the action ("Water Green 3 tonight"), then the reason.

Units: calls are shown only as run minutes; rain and ET in inches; °F and gallons; a space before every unit.

Data: never put API keys in the browser; use Supabase edge functions and secrets.

### **1\. App shell and design system**

Set up the app shell. Create the theme tokens from the project rules for light and dark mode, with a Display setting (Light / Dark / Automatic) stored per user. Add a bottom tab bar with Home, Zones, Map, Notes, Community (icons \+ labels), fixed above the home-bar safe area, for superintendents and crew; managers see Zones, Map, Water use. Settings opens from a profile button at the top right; for crew it holds only language, display and notifications. Create reusable components: StatusChip (water/hold/check), ConfidenceBars (1-3 bars \+ optional word), SoilWaterBar (fill with a threshold tick), InputRow (label, value, source, age, optional Default or Stale tag), Composer (64 px mic button with hold-to-talk and tap-to-toggle, waveform, timer, and a text field), FeedItem (user entry or FairFlow reply), ConfirmCard item row (icon, summary, large number, zone chip, edit, remove; amber variant with option chips), BottomSheet, PrimaryButton, SecondaryButton, Banner (info/warning), Toast, SkeletonRow, EmptyState. Build a /components preview page that shows each one in light and dark mode so we can review them on a phone.

### **2\. Database and sample data**

Create the Supabase tables with row-level security so users only see courses they belong to:  
\- courses (name, address, lat, lng, timezone, holes, water\_source nullable, controller\_brand nullable, map\_path nullable, water\_price\_per\_1000\_gal, crew\_can\_change\_calls boolean default false, water\_short boolean default false, turf\_priority JSON default \[greens, tees, fairways, rough\], is\_demo boolean default false)  
\- course\_members (course\_id, user\_id, role: superintendent \| crew \| manager, language: en \| es)  
\- zones (course\_id, hole\_number, name, turf\_type: greens\|tees\|fairways\|rough, map\_position JSON (x and y as % of the uploaded map), area\_sqft, soil: sand\|sandy\_loam\|loam\|clay\_loam\|clay, slope: flat\|gentle\|moderate\|steep, root\_depth\_in, each with a \*\_source: default\|user)  
\- valves (zone\_id, station text e.g. "3A", area\_sqft, precip\_rate\_in\_hr nullable, flow\_gpm nullable (one of the two required), soil and slope overrides nullable, is\_estimate boolean, flagged boolean, flag\_question text nullable, source: ai\|standard\|user)  
\- weather\_daily (course\_id, date, rain\_in, et\_ref\_in, forecast\_rain\_in, source, fetched\_at, is\_stale)  
\- recommendations (valve\_id, zone\_id, date, version, superseded boolean, status: water\|hold\|check, minutes\_low, minutes\_high, target\_in, confidence: low\|medium\|high, reason text, balance JSON {start\_pct, et\_in, rain\_in, irrigation\_in, end\_pct, threshold\_pct}, inputs JSON \[{name, value, unit, source, age\_hours, is\_default, is\_stale}\], settings JSON, engine\_version, flags JSON (too\_wet, rain\_missed, stays\_dry, trimmed\_for\_short\_water), created\_at)  
\- observations (course\_id, user\_id, created\_at, kind: log\|question, input: voice\|text, audio\_path, transcript, language, lat, lng, items JSON, status: pending\|confirmed\|cancelled\|answered, reply text, helpful boolean nullable)  
\- decisions (recommendation\_id, valve\_id, date, user\_id, action: follow\|override, new\_status, new\_minutes, reason, observation\_id, ran\_confirmed: yes\|no\|unknown default unknown)  
\- logs (course\_id, zone\_id nullable, valve\_id nullable, date, type: rain\|irrigation\|hand\_check, value, unit, user\_id, observation\_id)  
\- turf\_entries (zone\_id, date, condition: healthy\|slightly\_dry\|wilting\|dry\_spots\|too\_wet\|possible\_disease, note, photo\_path, user\_id, observation\_id)  
\- issues (course\_id, zone\_id, valve\_id nullable, observation\_id, author\_id, type: broken\_head\|leak\|dry\_spot\|wet\_spot\|other, note, photo\_path, lat, lng, status: open\|task\|done, assigned\_to, created\_at)  
\- criteria (course\_id, scope: turf\_type or zone\_id or valve\_id, threshold\_pct, depth\_per\_cycle\_in, rain\_credit\_in, no\_water\_days, source: default\|typed\|learned\_decisions\|learned\_turf\|map, set\_by user\_id nullable, updated\_at)  
\- suggestions (course\_id, scope, setting, current\_value, proposed\_value, evidence JSON, from\_user\_id, status: pending\|approved\|rejected)  
\- briefings (course\_id, date, text\_en, text\_es, updated\_at)  
\- change\_history (table\_name, row\_id, user\_id, changed\_at, before JSON, after JSON), written whenever an entry is edited or undone  
\- uploads (course\_id, kind: irrigation\|weather\|probe, file\_path, row\_count, errors JSON, created\_at), removable; removing one deletes its rows and recalculates  
\- probe\_readings (valve\_id, date, soil\_water\_pct, upload\_id)  
\- community\_posts (author\_id, course\_id, topic: irrigation\|turf\|equipment\|weather\|crew, title, body, photo\_path nullable, language, show\_course boolean default false, status: visible\|hidden, created\_at), readable by every superintendent and crew member on any FairFlow course; authors edit or delete their own  
\- community\_replies (post\_id, author\_id, body, language, status, created\_at)  
\- community\_helpful (reply\_id, user\_id), community\_reports (post\_id or reply\_id, user\_id, reason, created\_at)  
\- engine\_checks (run\_at, engine\_version, passed, results JSON)  
Roles: only superintendents write decisions, zones, valves, criteria and approve suggestions; crew insert observations, logs, turf\_entries, issues and suggestions; managers are read-only but can insert question observations. Seed a "Sample course" near Ann Arbor, MI with 6 zones (2 greens, 1 tee, 2 fairways, 1 rough), 2 to 3 valves each, 14 days of weather\_daily and recommendations, a few observations with replies, and a sample briefing.

### **3\. Sign in and roles (S1)**

Build S1 Sign in. Full-height screen: top half deep green with the FairFlow wordmark (serif) and the tagline "Know which zones need water before you leave the shop."; bottom half an ivory card with an email field (email keyboard), a primary button "Send me a sign-in link" using Supabase magic link, a divider, and "Continue with Google". Below, a "Try the demo" link that opens demo mode (prompt 16\) without signing in. After sending, show "Check your email on this phone" with the address and "Use a different email". Support invite links (/join/:token) that add the user to a course with a role and show "Join \[course\] as \[role\]" with one Join button. After sign-in: superintendent with no course goes to setup; superintendents and crew go to Home; managers go to Zones.

### **4\. Course details and map upload (S2)**

Build S2 as steps 1 and 2 of a 3-step setup. No map drawing anywhere. Setup must move both ways: the progress bar shows the step names (Details, Map, Check) and any step already reached is tappable to jump to it; every step after the first has a Back button and the phone's back gesture goes to the previous step; everything entered is saved to Supabase as it's typed, so nothing is lost moving around; a "Finish later" link saves progress, and reopening the app resumes at the same step.

Step 1, one screen: course name with search that fills in the address and lat/lng (call a free geocoding service such as OpenStreetMap Nominatim from an edge function, respecting its usage policy); number of holes as three large chips (9, 18, 27); and a collapsed optional section for water source (city, well, pond, reclaimed), water price per 1,000 gal and controller brand, with "Skip for now". Next.

Step 2: a large "Take a photo or upload" area accepting images and PDFs of an irrigation map, course layout or scorecard, saved to Supabase storage. Then call an edge function "read-map" that sends the image (each PDF page as an image) and the hole count to the Anthropic Messages API (Claude, vision) and asks for JSON only: for each hole, its zones (green, tee, fairway, rough) with turf type, position on the map (x and y as % of the image), estimated area in sq ft when a scale or known dimensions allow, valve or station labels when printed, and a confidence (high or low) with a short question for anything unsure. Save holes, zones and valves with source "ai", is\_estimate true for areas and output, and flagged true for low-confidence items. Show progress ("Reading your map… found 12 holes so far"). If reading fails, or the user taps "No map? Use a standard layout", create a green, tee and fairway zone per hole with one valve each, using placeholder typical areas from a constants file, all marked as estimates.

### **5\. Check your course (S3)**

Build S3 Check your course (step 3 of 3). Header "Here's your course" with totals (holes, zones, valves). At the top, an amber card "N things to check" listing each flagged item as a one-tap question with chip answers ("Hole 7 green: 2 or 3 valves?"); answering clears the flag. Below, holes as collapsible rows ("Hole 1 · 6 valves · Green, tee, fairway"); tapping one allows edits to zone names, turf type, soil and slope pickers, and each valve's station, area (sq ft) and sprinkler output (in/hr or gpm). Areas and output show an "Estimate" tag until changed, with a hint on where to find output: controller program, irrigation map or nozzle chart. Corrections can also be spoken or typed ("Hole 7 green has three valves") through the same parse-and-confirm flow. An optional "Add more data" card offers irrigation history, weather station or rain gauge, and soil probe CSV uploads, with Skip; with none, FairFlow runs on open data. Primary button "Looks right" runs fetch-weather and run-engine for the first time and opens Home. Everything stays editable later in Settings \> Course, including re-uploading a map. If the user goes back and changes the hole count or uploads a different map, re-run read-map, keep every fix the user already made, and flag only what changed.

### **5a. Weather data function**

Create a Supabase edge function "fetch-weather". For each course, call the Open-Meteo API (no key needed) with the course's lat, lng and timezone for daily precipitation and FAO-56 reference evapotranspiration (et0) for the past 14 days and the next 3 days. Convert millimetres to inches where needed (1 in \= 25.4 mm). Upsert into weather\_daily with source "Open-Meteo" and fetched\_at. If the call fails, keep the last values and set is\_stale \= true. Schedule it daily at 4:30 am course time, and add a "Refresh weather" button with the last fetch time on Settings \> Data.

### **5b. Engine and recommendation records**

Create a Supabase edge function "run-engine" with ENGINE\_VERSION \= "0.1" at the top. Keep all the math in this one function, with no UI code, and the constants in one clearly labeled block at the top. Starting constants are placeholders for our team to review with a superintendent:  
\- water-holding (in per in of root depth): sand 0.06, sandy loam 0.10, loam 0.15, clay loam 0.18, clay 0.20  
\- default root depth (in): greens 4, tees 5, fairways 6, rough 8  
\- turf coefficient: greens 0.8, tees 0.8, fairways 0.75, rough 0.7  
\- slope factor on rain: flat 1.0, gentle 0.9, moderate 0.75, steep 0.6  
\- default threshold: 50% of capacity; refill target: 85% of capacity; new valves start at 70%  
For each valve and date: capacity \= root depth × water-holding; effective rain \= rain × slope factor (spoken, typed or station rain replaces weather rain; a probe reading for a valve's date replaces its estimated soil water); soil water \= yesterday − ET × turf coefficient \+ effective rain \+ irrigation, capped between 0 and capacity. A followed recommendation counts as irrigation applied once confirmed (decisions.ran\_confirmed \= yes); an irrigation log for that valve and date overrides it; if still unknown at the morning run, count it but lower that valve's confidence one step. Status: water if soil water is below the threshold, or will be after tomorrow's ET with under 0.05 in forecast rain; hold if not, or if forecast rain covers the gap; check if any input is stale or missing. A logged value that differs from weather data is used as is and is never a reason for check. A valve whose area or output is still an estimate gets one confidence level lower. Target inches \= refill target − soil water. Run minutes \= target × area × 60 / (96.3 × flow gpm), or target / precip rate × 60; show a range of ±15%, rounded to whole minutes; on moderate or steep slopes, say "split into two runs". Write one recommendations row per valve per day with the balance, an inputs snapshot (value, source, age), settings used and ENGINE\_VERSION. Never update a row: if a past day changes, insert a new version and mark the old one superseded. Flags: if soil water is at capacity after rain, status hold with reason "too wet"; if a hold was based on forecast rain that didn't fall, catch up on the next run and set rain\_missed so the briefing says so; if a valve stays below threshold for 3 or more days despite followed runs, status check with reason "stays dry: likely a head or line problem". When courses.water\_short is on, keep turf types higher in turf\_priority at full target and trim lower ones first (fairways to half, rough to hold, adjustable constants), tagging trimmed\_for\_short\_water. Run it after fetch-weather on the schedule, after every confirmed observation (for affected valves, from that day forward), and on demand if today's rows are missing when the app opens.

### **5c. Engine check page (S15)**

Build S15 Engine check, reachable from Settings \> Data for superintendents only. Store three test cases next to the engine: a sand green, a loam fairway and a clay rough, each with fixed inputs (soil, slope, root depth, area, flow, yesterday's soil water, ET, rain, irrigation) and the expected soil water, status and run minutes that our team calculates by hand. A Run check button sends them through run-engine without saving recommendations and shows expected vs actual for each, with Pass (within 0.01 in and 1 minute) or Fail. Save each run to engine\_checks with the engine version. If the latest check failed, show a warning banner on Settings.

### **6\. Home: talk or type (S4) and Zones list (S14)**

Build S4 Home, the start screen for superintendents. Deep green header with course name, date and "Updated \[time\]". At the top of the feed, the briefing card from the briefings table in the user's language, with zone names as links and "Updated \[time\]" when it has refreshed during the day. After a night with runs, it starts with "Did last night's runs go as planned?" and a one-tap "Yes, all ran" button that sets ran\_confirmed \= yes on last night's followed decisions (the mic handles exceptions like "3B didn't run"), and under it "Water 4 · Hold 11 · Check 2 · See all zones" (zones counted by their most urgent valve). Below, a conversation feed of today's observations, questions and FairFlow's replies, newest at the bottom: each confirmed entry shows who logged it and a short summary; tap to edit or undo at any time, keeping the change history and recalculating from that day. Mac's briefing, replies and answers show his avatar; tapping it opens an "About Mac" bottom sheet (AI watering advisor; uses your records plus public weather and soil data; ask where any number came from; no disease or chemical advice). Answers to questions show thumbs up and down. Prompt chips above the composer: "Rain in the gauge?", "How do the greens look?", "What changed since yesterday?". Composer docked above the tab bar: the 64 px mic (hold to talk, or tap to start and stop) using MediaRecorder with a waveform and timer, and a text field "Tell Mac or ask anything" that sends on Return and works with the phone keyboard's dictation. A small "Use a form instead" link opens the Quick log sheet. For now, on send, show a placeholder confirm sheet; prompts 10 and 10a wire up the real flow.

Also build S14 Zones list: summary counts that filter the list; zones grouped Check, Water, Hold by their most urgent valve; 64 px rows with StatusChip, zone name, run time range in minutes, one-line reason, ConfidenceBars and a valve count; swipe right to Follow all of that zone's valves (one decision per valve, undo toast); tap to open Zone detail; a map button. Managers land on S14, read-only, with the composer for questions only. Skeleton rows while loading; keep the last data in local storage so both screens reopen instantly.

### **7\. Zone detail (S6)**

Build S6 Zone detail. Top: back arrow, zone name, StatusChip (most urgent valve) and ConfidenceBars with the word. A Valves list: one row per valve with station, StatusChip and run time range ("3A · Water · 8 to 12 min"); swipe a row to Follow that valve; tap to select it. For the selected valve, a "Show the math" card read from the recommendation's balance field: "47% − 0.21 in ET \+ 0.10 in rain \+ 0 irrigation \= 41%" against the threshold, with the SoilWaterBar. A track record line "Agreed with you on X of Y days" computed from recommendations and decisions. Inputs list using InputRow from the recommendation's inputs snapshot; tapping any number opens "Where's this from?" with its source, date and who set it, plus Change and Ask Mac. A "Raise confidence" list. History: a 14-day soil water line per valve (Recharts) with markers for turf entries, overrides and notes; tapping a day opens that day's stored recommendation. An "Ask about this zone" button opens the composer with the zone filled in. Sticky bottom bar: Follow all valves (primary) and Override (secondary), equal width. Crew and managers see no Follow or Override.

### **8\. Override and Quick log sheets (S7, S8)**

Build two bottom sheets. Override (S7): valve chips (all valves in the zone selected by default), status chips (Water, Hold, Check), a run time stepper in 1-minute steps, reason chips (Looks drier, Event tomorrow, Forecast is wrong, Other), an optional mic for a spoken reason, and Save, which writes a decision and shows "Logged. FairFlow will learn from this." Quick log (S8): four tabs. Rain: inches on a decimal keypad, whole course or chosen zones, default today. Irrigation: minutes or inches per zone. Hand check: three large buttons Drier / As expected / Wetter. Turf: six large condition buttons (Healthy, Slightly dry, Wilting, Dry spots, Too wet, Possible disease), optional photo (camera) and note. Each saves in one tap with a toast.

### **9\. Map view (S5)**

Build S5 Map. Use the course's uploaded map as the base and mark each zone at its map\_position with a pin showing its status color, icon and word, so it reads without color. Show open issues as pins. Tapping a zone opens a compact bottom card (status, amount, reason) that expands into Zone detail. A layer toggle offers Status, Confidence and Regional wetness (context only). Add a toggle to a satellite view of the course location, remembered per user. Use a darker basemap in dark mode.

### **10\. Understand and confirm (S9)**

Build the understand-and-confirm flow behind the Home composer.

1\. When recording stops, upload the audio to Supabase storage and call an edge function "transcribe" (leave a clearly marked placeholder for the speech-to-text provider and key). Typed text skips this step.  
2\. Call an edge function "parse-observation". It sends the transcript, the course's zone names and turf types, the user's role, today's date and the phone's location to the Anthropic Messages API (Claude), with a system prompt that returns ONLY JSON: {"items":\[{"type":"rain\|irrigation\|hand\_check\|turf\|issue\|override\|note","zones":\[zone ids\] or "all" or a turf type,"value":number,"unit":"in\|min","date":"YYYY-MM-DD","condition":...,"issue\_type":...,"status":...,"reason":...,"confidence":"high\|low","question":optional,"options":optional}\]}. The model must never calculate water amounts; it only extracts what was said. Include valve names in what is sent so items can name a valve ("3B"). If the message is a question rather than an observation, return {"question": true} and send it to ask-advisor (prompt 10a) instead of opening the confirm card. Keep the API key in Supabase secrets.  
3\. Save an observations row (status pending) and open S9 "Here's what I heard" as a bottom sheet: the transcript collapsed at the top (tap to edit and re-parse); one row per item with icon, plain summary, large numbers and a zone chip, each with edit and remove; low-confidence items as amber rows with option chips ("Which green? 1 · 3 · 7"); flag out-of-range values (rain over 3 in, irrigation over 60 min). For crew, override items read "Suggest to superintendent" unless courses.crew\_can\_change\_calls is on.  
4\. Confirm (full width, 56 px) writes each item to its table (logs, turf\_entries, issues, decisions, or suggestions for crew), marks the observation confirmed, and shows FairFlow's reply in the feed in one or two lines naming what changed: "Got it. Green 3 moves to Water, 8 to 12 minutes tonight." Until the real engine exists, build the reply from the items and the new recommendations from run-engine. Cancel discards. If a spoken value disagrees with the weather data, use the person's value and mention the gap in the reply ("Got it, 0.50 in. The weather data showed 0.10 in, so I'm using yours."). Detect English or Spanish automatically and write the reply in the user's chosen language. If Read replies aloud is on in Settings, speak the reply with the browser's speech synthesis.  
5\. While waiting, the feed shows "Listening…" then "Working it out…"; target under 3 seconds. Offline: keep audio and text in IndexedDB with "Saved on phone · waiting for signal", and process automatically when back online.

### **10a. Morning briefing and Ask the advisor**

Create two edge functions that call the Anthropic Messages API (Claude), with the key in Supabase secrets.

1\. "write-briefing": after the morning run-engine, and again whenever a confirmed entry, an override or a new crew issue changes today's calls, send today's recommendations (zone, valve, status, minutes, reason, confidence), open issues and pending suggestions. Ask for a 2 to 4 sentence briefing in Mac's voice: a calm retired superintendent speaking in the first person: the zones that need water with minutes per valve, anything to check and why, anything new, then "Everything else holds." Use only numbers from the data. Save English and Spanish versions to briefings. Home shows the user's language at the top of the feed, with tappable zone names.

2\. "ask-advisor": when parse-observation marks a message as a question, send the question, the user's language, and the relevant records: today's and up to 14 days of recommendations, inputs, decisions, logs and turf entries for the zones mentioned, or a course summary. Ask for a 2 to 3 sentence answer that quotes numbers with their sources, links zones, answers questions about assumptions with their source, date and who set it ("Where did the 45% come from?"), says plainly when the records can't answer, declines disease, fertility and pesticide questions, and never changes a call. Before showing it, check that every number in the answer appears in the records sent; if one doesn't, show "I can't answer that from the records" instead. Show the answer in the feed with thumbs up and down, saved to observations.helpful.

### **11\. Notes and issues, and Crew home (S10, S11)**

Build S10 Notes and issues: filter chips (Open, Mine, Zone, Type), then cards for each issue and unplaced note with author, time, zone, type, transcript preview and an audio play button. Superintendents can swipe to mark done, or tap Make task to assign a crew member (sends them a push if alerts are on). Build S11 Crew home for crew: the same composer and feed as Home showing their own entries, their assigned tasks, and a short list of zones marked water or check today labeled "hand-water" or "check". Crew confirms save logs, turf entries and issues; any override item becomes a suggestion to the superintendent. No Follow or Override buttons.

### **11b. Community (S16, S17)**

Build the Community tab for superintendents and crew (managers don't see it). S16 board: topic chips (All, Irrigation, Turf, Equipment, Weather, Crew), a search field, and post cards with title, author role and area ("Superintendent · Saline"), reply count and Helpful count. Never show a course name unless the author turned on "Show my course name". A "New post" button opens a bottom sheet: title, details (typed, or spoken through the same mic as Home), topic, optional photo, and the course name switch (off by default). S17 thread: the post, then replies oldest first, each with Helpful (one per user) and Report; a reply composer with text and mic. Posts and replies in a language other than the reader's show "Translate", which calls an edge function that sends the text to the Anthropic API and shows the translation under the original. Reported items are hidden after review by the team; add a simple admin list of reports. Show an in-app banner on Home when someone replies to your post. Mac never reads or cites Community posts.

### **12\. Settings and My criteria (S12)**

Build S12 Settings as a grouped list: My criteria, Team, Data, Notifications, Water use, Display, Sign out. My criteria: a "Water is short" switch (also settable by voice from Home, through the confirm card) and a drag-to-order turf priority (greens, tees, fairways, rough by default); per turf type and zone, show threshold %, depth per cycle, rain credit, no-water days, each tagged with its source (Default, Typed, Learned from your decisions, Learned from turf notes), with edit, undo and reset. Show pending suggestions as cards with the plain-language proposal ("You tend to water at 45%. Use 45%?"), the evidence entries in an expandable list described as a pattern, not proof, and Approve / Not now. Team: invite by email or share a link per role, change role, remove, and a "Crew can change calls" switch (off by default, so crew changes become suggestions). Data: optional uploads (irrigation history, weather station or rain gauge exports, soil probe readings) with column mapping, row-level errors, which valves each improves, and Remove; source status with last update; units toggle. Display: light, dark or automatic; language (English or Español); Read replies aloud (off by default). Notifications: alerts on/off, quiet hours, mid-morning nudge on/off and time (default 10 am).

### **13\. Water use (S13)**

Build S13 Water use, visible to superintendents (from Settings) and managers (as a tab). Top: this season's gallons and estimated cost (per valve, from run minutes and flow for followed calls and logged irrigation, at the course water price), with change vs last season when data exists; label estimated figures. A weekly bar chart of gallons (Recharts) filterable by turf type and zone. A Decisions panel: % followed vs overridden and top override reasons. Export CSV and PDF buttons. Read-only for managers.

### **14\. Install to home screen and offline**

Make FairFlow installable: add a web app manifest (name FairFlow, deep green theme color, ivory background, icons 192 and 512, standalone display) and a one-time "Add FairFlow to your home screen" card with iPhone (Share, Add to Home Screen) and Android instructions. Keep the last briefing and calls in local storage so they show instantly on reopen. With no signal, keep unsent entries on the phone while the app is open, label them "Waiting for signal", and send them automatically when back online. Do not add a service worker yet.

### **15\. In-app alerts**

Add in-app alerts only (no email or push yet). After the morning run, if at least one valve is water or check, show a banner at the top of Home and Zones until the superintendent opens the briefing. At the nudge time (default 10 am, adjustable), if nobody on the course has logged anything that day, show one banner on Home: "Nothing logged yet today. Anything to report?" When a task is assigned to a crew member, show a banner on their Crew home. Respect quiet hours. Settings \> Notifications has alerts on/off, quiet hours and the nudge time.

### **16\. Demo mode (S18)**

Build demo mode. Seed a fictional course "Pine Hollow (demo)" (courses.is\_demo \= true) with 18 holes, 2 to 3 valves per zone, 30 days of stored demo weather, recommendations, decisions, logs, turf entries, issues and a few Community posts (read-only in the demo). Entry points: a "Try the demo" link on S1; a shareable URL /demo that needs no sign-in (an anonymous session on a fresh copy of the demo course, deleted after 24 hours); and the team's test login. Show S18: an amber banner on every screen, "Demo course · nothing here is real". Tapping it opens a controls sheet: View as (Superintendent, Crew, Manager), switching the role in place; Scenario chips (Dry spell, Heavy rain, Broken head, Tournament) that load matching weather, logs and issues; "Next morning", which moves the demo date ahead one day and reruns run-engine and write-briefing using the stored demo weather, not the live API; and "Reset demo", which restores day 1\. Mac answers from the demo data. Demo sessions must never read or write real courses: enforce this in row-level security, not only in the UI.

## **Building the hard parts in Lovable, and phone testing**

Lovable builds every part, so each hard part needs a way to check it without reading code.

| Part | How Lovable builds it | How you check it |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Water balance engine (F4) | One versioned edge function, prompt 5b | Engine check page (S15) and the "show the math" card |
| Weather data (F2) | Edge function calling Open-Meteo, prompt 5a | Last fetch time and source on Settings \> Data |
| Daily 5:30 am run | Supabase scheduled function; on-demand fallback when the app opens | "Updated" time on Home |
| Recommendation records (F16) | Insert-only rows with versions | Tap a past day in Zone detail and compare with what you saw then |
| Transcription | Phone keyboard dictation first; in-app mic through a transcription API in an edge function | Read the transcript on the confirm card |
| Parsing, briefing and answers (F12, F17) | Edge functions calling Claude with JSON-only replies | A list of 20 test sentences and 10 test questions with expected results, rerun after changes |
| Learning suggestions (F10, F13) | Simple rules in an edge function | The evidence list on each suggestion |
| In-app alerts (F15) | Banners driven by today's records and logs | Compare the banners with the Zones list |

**Keep it testable.** Tell Lovable to keep the engine in one file with no UI code, never to change it while building screens, and to bump the engine version whenever it does change. If a screen prompt breaks the engine check, roll back with Lovable's version history rather than prompting around it. Work out the three engine check examples by hand in a spreadsheet first, using the constants in prompt 5b.

**Phone test checklist after each prompt**

* ☐ Opens and reads correctly on an iPhone and an Android phone, not just a desktop browser  
* ☐ Nothing hidden under the notch or home bar; keyboard doesn't cover the field being typed in  
* ☐ Every button reachable and tappable with one thumb  
* ☐ Readable outside in direct sun (light mode) and at dawn (dark mode)  
* ☐ Status readable with color turned off (phone grayscale setting)  
* ☐ Works on a weak connection; Today and voice notes work in airplane mode  
* ☐ Large system text setting doesn't break layouts
